result.question:
Assess the NOVELTY, as of June 2026, of this earthquake-forecasting result so I can decide a target journal. The result: a neural marked spatio-temporal point process (selective-SSM whole-catalog encoder + flow-matching/rectified-flow temporal head + ETAS-shaped, observation-anchored spatial & Gutenberg-Richter magnitude heads) that (a) beats the ETAS model on TEMPORAL log-likelihood with multi-seed significance across all 5 California EarthquakeNPP catalogs, and (b) — the headline — pre-trained on one region, TRANSFERS across tectonic regimes (transform/subduction/extension/collision; California, Japan, Chile, Greece, Iran) and after brief FEW-SHOT fine-tuning beats REGION-FITTED ETAS on temporal forecasting in every regime, including data-poor regions where training from scratch fails and ETAS (which must be inverted per region) has no transfer mechanism. ETAS still wins spatial/total likelihood.

Determine, with specific cited papers (titles, authors, year, venue), for each sub-claim whether our result is (a) FIRST/novel, (b) a significant extension of existing work, or (c) already done:

1. TRANSFER LEARNING for earthquake FORECASTING (rate/intensity/point-process likelihood), zero-shot or few-shot, cross-region or cross-tectonic-regime. CRITICAL: distinguish forecasting from phase-picking / detection / denoising / magnitude estimation / ground-motion, where transfer learning IS well established and does NOT count. Has anyone shown a neural forecasting model transfer across regions and beat locally-fit ETAS?
2. "Foundation model for seismicity / earthquake forecasting" — any pre-trained, transferable/adaptable model aimed at forecasting (not detection). e.g. SeisLM, Seismic foundation models, global/transfer ETAS-replacement neural models. What do they actually do?
3. Neural point processes vs ETAS for earthquake forecasting, 2022-2026: the EarthquakeNPP benchmark (Stockman et al.) and ANY NPP shown to beat ETAS on temporal or total log-likelihood with statistical significance across multiple catalogs.
4. Data-efficiency claim: any neural earthquake-forecasting model shown to beat locally-fit ETAS specifically in small-catalog / data-poor regions via transfer.
5. The mechanistic finding that conditioning output heads on a global whole-catalog embedding causes memorization (train LL collapses, test LL explodes) in neural earthquake models.

Deliverable: a clear novelty verdict per sub-claim; which claims are safe to call "first"; the single strongest novel contribution; and given that novelty, the highest-prestige realistic venue (Nature / Nature Geoscience / Nature Communications / Science Advances / GRL / JGR Solid Earth / Seismica / SRL). Be skeptical and adversarial — actively hunt for prior work that would sink the novelty claim, especially 2024-2026 preprints on EarthArXiv/arXiv about transfer learning or foundation models for earthquake forecasting.
result.summary: As of June 2026, the strongest and safest novel contribution is the headline: a neural marked spatio-temporal point process that is pre-trained on one region and, via few-shot fine-tuning, beats REGION-FITTED ETAS on point-process TEMPORAL log-likelihood across distinct tectonic regimes (CA/Japan/Chile/Greece/Iran) — including data-poor regions where ETAS has no transfer mechanism. No prior work demonstrates cross-tectonic-regime transfer of a neural POINT-PROCESS forecaster that beats locally-fit ETAS on likelihood: the closest prior arts are RECAST (which only PROPOSES multi-region transfer as future aspiration, never demonstrates it) and SafeNet (which does cross-region transfer for forecasting and beats ETAS, but as a gridded annual-max-magnitude CLASSIFIER scored on F1/recall, NOT a point-process likelihood — a categorically different model class). The secondary claim — a neural model beating ETAS on temporal log-likelihood with multi-seed significance across all five California EarthquakeNPP catalogs — is also strongly differentiated, because the canonical TMLR 2026 benchmark established that none of five NPPs beat ETAS, and the only near-contemporaries (FERN ties ETAS; Zhan et al. NMRP only "matches/sometimes surpasses" temporally, no spatial head, no transfer, no multi-seed significance) fall short of a clean, significance-tested, multi-catalog win. The honest concession that ETAS still wins spatial/total likelihood is fully consistent with the benchmark (ETAS dominates spatial LL against every NPP), so the temporal-axis win is the defensible novel margin. Recommended target: Nature Communications or Nature Geoscience for the transfer/foundation-model headline (with Science Advances as an alternative); if reviewers push back on prestige, JGR Solid Earth, GRL, or the domain-native Seismica are realistic fallbacks. The single must-have framing guardrail: claim "first for neural point-process / point-process-likelihood forecasting," NOT "first transfer learning for earthquake forecasting" unqualified, because SafeNet preempts the broad version.

findings.claim: Sub-claim 1 (cross-region/cross-regime transfer for forecasting that beats locally-fit ETAS): NOVEL for the neural POINT-PROCESS / likelihood class, but NOT 'first transfer learning for earthquake forecasting' unqualified. SafeNet (Zhang et al. 2025) already did cross-region few-shot transfer for forecasting and beat ETAS, but only as a gridded annual-max-magnitude CLASSIFIER on F1/recall — not a point-process likelihood. RECAST only proposed multi-region transfer as future aspiration; it never demonstrated it.
sources: Zhang et al. (2025), 'Scalable intermediate-term earthquake forecasting with multimodal fusion neural networks' (SafeNet), Scientific Reports, 10.1038/s41598-025-93877-7 / PMC11928507

Dascher-Cousineau, Shchur, Brodsky, Gunnemann (2023), 'Using Deep Learning for Flexible and Scalable Earthquake Forecasting' (RECAST), Geophysical Research Letters 50(17), e2023GL103909, 10.1029/2023GL103909
Stockman, Lawson, Werner (2024/2026), 'EarthquakeNPP: A Benchmark for Earthquake Forecasting with Neural Point Processes', arXiv:2410.08226, TMLR 2026
findings.evidence: SafeNet was pre-trained on a 50-year China catalog and few-shot fine-tuned on 3 years of U.S. data, then forecast the Contiguous/Western U.S., recalling 21/40 M>=6 regions vs ETAS 11 — a genuine cross-region, cross-tectonic-regime transfer FORECASTING result that beats locally-applied ETAS. BUT it is a 4x4-degree gridded annual maximum-magnitude classifier (4 magnitude classes per region per year) evaluated only with accuracy/precision/recall/macro-F1; it reports NO log-likelihood, NO intensity function, NO marked point-process formulation. RECAST's cross-region transfer exists only as press-release aspiration ('We might be able to train on New Zealand, Japan, California...'); the paper itself is synthetic + Southern California only with no transfer experiment. Therefore the defensible novelty is narrowed precisely: first NEURAL POINT-PROCESS forecaster to transfer across tectonic regimes and beat region-fitted ETAS on point-process temporal log-likelihood. The user must NOT claim 'first transfer learning for earthquake forecasting' without the point-process qualifier, or SafeNet sinks it.

findings.claim: Sub-claim 2 ('foundation model for seismicity / forecasting'): NOVEL as aimed at point-process forecasting. The existing 'foundation model'-branded earthquake works do NOT do transferable point-process forecasting. MultiFoundationQuake uses generic non-seismic time-series FMs (TimeGPT/Chronos/PatchTST/iTransformer/TSMixer pre-trained on weather/traffic/M4) for deterministic energy regression in one region; SeisLM is a seismic-waveform FM but does detection/phase-picking, not forecasting.
sources: Jafari, Fox, Rundle, Donnellan, Grant Ludwig (2024), 'Time Series Foundation Models and Deep Learning Architectures for Earthquake Temporal and Spatial Nowcasting' (MultiFoundationQuake), arXiv:2408.11990v1 / MDPI GeoHazards 5(4):59

Liu et al. (2024), 'SeisLM: a Foundation Model for Seismic Waveforms', arXiv:2410.15765, NeurIPS 2024 (referenced in claim [4] verification as the actual seismic FM, which does detection/picking not forecasting)
findings.evidence: MultiFoundationQuake forecasts cumulative released energy per 0.1-degree bin over 14 days as deterministic time-series regression (metrics: NNSE/MSE/MAE), reports NO point-process likelihood, makes NO ETAS likelihood comparison (defers ETAS to 'a later study'), is confined to Southern California, and its 'foundation models' are generic non-seismic TSFMs pre-trained on weather/traffic/M4 — cross-DOMAIN, not cross-region. SeisLM is pre-trained on seismic data but targets event detection, phase-picking, onset-time regression, foreshock-aftershock classification — explicitly NOT forecasting/rate/point-process likelihood. So no existing seismicity-specific pretrained model is aimed at transferable point-process FORECASTING; the user's model occupies an open niche. Caveat: transfer learning IS well established for phase-picking/detection/denoising/magnitude/ground-motion — those do not count and must be explicitly distinguished in the paper.

findings.claim: Sub-claim 3 (NPP beats ETAS on temporal/total log-likelihood with multi-seed significance across all 5 California catalogs): NOVEL as a clean, significance-tested, multi-catalog temporal WIN. The canonical EarthquakeNPP benchmark (TMLR 2026) established that NONE of five NPPs (NSTPP, DeepSTPP, AutoSTPP, DSTPP, SMASH) outperform ETAS, and ETAS holds the highest temporal log-likelihood; NPPs are only 'comparable or marginally better' in isolated cases without significance testing.
sources: Stockman, Lawson, Werner (2024/2026), 'EarthquakeNPP', arXiv:2410.08226 (v1-v3) / TMLR 03/2026, OpenReview dIcNAg6ZuZ

Werner, Stockman, Tian, Zhang (2025), 'Benchmarking and Adapting Neural Point Processes for Operational Earthquake Forecasting in California and China', SCEC Annual Meeting Poster #208, central.scec.org/publication/14827
findings.evidence: EarthquakeNPP states verbatim 'none of the five tested NPP implementations outperform ETAS' and 'ETAS consistently achieves the highest temporal log-likelihood,' concluding current NPPs are 'not yet suitable for practical earthquake forecasting.' The EarthquakeNPP group's own Sept 2025 SCEC follow-up reports generative NPPs 'consistently underperform' on catalog metrics and likelihood-based NPPs show only 'marginal temporal information gains over USGS forecasts' (NOT over ETAS) — no clean ETAS win is claimed. IMPORTANT NUANCE: the benchmark concedes NPPs are 'comparably or in some cases marginally better, except at the higher magnitude thresholds of the SCEDC catalog,' so isolated marginal NPP edges exist WITHOUT multi-seed significance. The user's novelty therefore rests specifically on (a) the rigor of multi-seed statistical significance and (b) consistency across ALL five catalogs — not on 'no NPP ever nudged ahead anywhere.' This framing should be stated precisely. Background context (not refutations): RECAST is only 'comparable to or better' on large S. California catalogs; Stockman et al. 2023 Central Apennines NPP-beats-ETAS is a single Italian sequence at lowered magnitude threshold (M1.2) where ETAS is penalized by incompleteness — not a multi-catalog significance-tested temporal win.

findings.claim: Closest temporal-axis competitor to sub-claim 3 is Zhan et al. (2026) NMRP, which 'matches and in some cases surpasses' temporal ETAS on the EarthquakeNPP California benchmark — but it has NO spatial head, does NO cross-region transfer, and does not report multi-seed significance across all catalogs, so it does not preempt the user's clean significance-tested multi-catalog win nor the transfer headline.
sources: Zhan et al. (2026), 'Flexible Seismicity Modeling With Neural Modulated Renewal Processes' (NMRP: NRP/I-NMRP/M-NMRP/J-NMRP), Earth's Future, 10.1029/2025EF007342 (published April 2026)
findings.evidence: NMRP abstract: 'I-NMRP and J-NMRP not only match, but in some cases surpass, ETAS in terms of log-likelihood, while requiring substantially less historical data.' It is a temporal/magnitude modulated renewal process (no spatial/location likelihood head), evaluated only on the EarthquakeNPP California benchmark (no Japan/Chile/Greece/Iran study regions), with its own future-work section flagging spatiotemporal and multi-region extensions as not-yet-done. The hedged 'match and in some cases surpass' is weaker than a clean significance-tested win across all five catalogs. This is the most direct competitor on the temporal-LL axis and MUST be cited and explicitly differentiated (the user has a spatial head, cross-regime transfer, and — claimed — significance), but it does not preempt either headline.

findings.claim: The honest concession that ETAS still wins spatial/total likelihood is fully consistent with the established baseline and does NOT weaken novelty — it sharpens it. The EarthquakeNPP benchmark shows ETAS consistently outperforms ALL NPPs on spatial log-likelihood, so the spatial/total frontier remaining ETAS-dominated is the published state of the art; the temporal-axis transfer win is the clean novel margin.
findings.evidence: Benchmark states verbatim 'ETAS consistently outperforms all NPPs in spatial log-likelihood'; the best NPP (AutoSTPP, anisotropic Hawkes kernels) only achieves highest spatial LL AMONG NPPs, still below ETAS. The 2026 SCEC follow-up corroborates no NPP surpasses ETAS on spatial or total LL. Conceding spatial/total to ETAS therefore aligns the paper with the canonical result and positions the temporal-only transfer win as the defensible advance, rather than overclaiming a total-likelihood victory that reviewers would reject.

findings.claim: Sub-claim 4 (data-efficiency: beating locally-fit ETAS in small/data-poor regions via TRANSFER): NOVEL for the cross-region-transfer mechanism. Prior NPP work either fails or wins only via in-region mechanisms. FERN (2023) only TIES ETAS (FERN+ gains 4-12% via sub-Mc magnitudes, all per-region training, no transfer); Zhan NMRP's data-efficiency is in-region renewal conditioning (~10 recent events), not cross-region transfer.
sources: Zlydenko et al. (2023), 'A neural encoder for earthquake rate forecasting' (FERN/FERN+), Scientific Reports 13, 10.1038/s41598-023-38033-9 / PMC10390553
Zhan et al. (2026), 'Flexible Seismicity Modeling With Neural Modulated Renewal Processes', Earth's Future, 10.1029/2025EF007342
Dascher-Cousineau et al. (2023), RECAST, GRL e2023GL103909
findings.evidence: FERN: 'FERN exhibits a comparable log-likelihood score to that of ETAS' — only a TIE; FERN+ gains 4-12% information per earthquake by ingesting sub-completeness magnitudes, NOT by transfer; all models trained separately per region (all sub-regions of one Japan subduction zone), no zero-shot/few-shot/cross-region evaluation. Zhan NMRP achieves data-efficiency via in-region renewal-process reformulation needing only ~10 recent events, explicitly NOT cross-region transfer (this is a COMPETING in-region data-efficiency result for sub-claim 4, but a different mechanism). RECAST actually performs WORSE than ETAS in small catalogs (it needs >~10^4 events to beat ETAS) — the opposite of data-efficiency-via-transfer. So the specific claim — neural forecaster rescuing data-poor regions where from-scratch training fails, via cross-tectonic-regime transfer, beating region-fit ETAS — is unclaimed in the NPP literature. Note: the broad version is partially preempted by SafeNet (transfer rescues data-poor U.S. forecasting), so again scope to point-process likelihood.

findings.claim: Sub-claim 5 (mechanistic finding: conditioning output heads on a global whole-catalog embedding causes memorization — train LL collapses, test LL explodes): NO prior-art source was found for or against this specific mechanistic finding in the verified literature, so on the available evidence it appears UNCLAIMED, but novelty cannot be affirmatively confirmed because no source addressed it.
sources: (No source in the verified claim set addresses this mechanism; absence-of-evidence only — see project memory file flowquake-build-state.md / spatial-gap-ceiling.md for the user's own internal finding)
findings.evidence: None of the 21 verified claims or refuted claims touch the global-embedding-causes-memorization mechanism. The surrounding NPP literature (EarthquakeNPP, RECAST, FERN, NMRP, MultiFoundationQuake, SafeNet) does not report a whole-catalog-embedding memorization failure mode. This is consistent with it being a genuinely novel mechanistic contribution, but the research did not surface a paper that confirms OR refutes it, so confidence is low and it should be framed as a methodological/diagnostic novelty rather than a literature-validated 'first.' A targeted search of 2024-2026 NPP/seismicity preprints and the general 'global conditioning causes memorization in autoregressive/conditional generative models' ML literature is advisable before claiming it as first.
findings.vote: no claim survived on this sub-question (absence in verified set)

findings.claim: Other 2024-2026 benchmark/dataset works (EPBench, May 2025) do NOT preempt either headline: EPBench is a multi-region dataset but trains/evaluates each region separately (no transfer), uses classification metrics (MR/FAR/MSE) not log-likelihood, and concludes no neural model satisfactorily beats ETAS. Its contemporaneous absence supports the user's novelty.
sources: EPBench (2025), 'EPBench: A Benchmark for Short-term Earthquake Prediction with Neural Networks', arXiv:2505.15588
findings.evidence: EPBench uses six worldwide regions but each is 'trained, predicted, and evaluated separately' — a multi-region dataset is NOT a transfer demonstration; zero mentions of transfer/few-shot/zero-shot/pre-train/foundation/cross-region. Metrics are Matching/Miss Rate, False Alarm Rate, spatio-temporal MSE, magnitude discrepancy — no log-likelihood. Its neural models (EP-CNN/LSTM/Transformer/Diff) are general time-series regressors, not point processes. It concludes neither ETAS nor neural nets are satisfactory. So this contemporaneous benchmark is corroborating context for novelty, not prior art. Caveat: this only proves EPBench specifically does not do these things, not that NO paper does — the comprehensive check rests on the EarthquakeNPP + SafeNet + NMRP + MultiFoundationQuake set above.

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity: this is a fast-moving field (EarthquakeNPP only accepted to TMLR in March 2026; Zhan NMRP published April 2026), so a final pre-submission literature sweep of EarthArXiv/arXiv (May-June 2026) is essential before claiming any 'first.' Source quality is generally high (primary peer-reviewed journals and the canonical TMLR benchmark), with two softer sources: the SCEC 2025 poster (conference abstract, but corroborated by the peer-reviewed benchmark) and the RECAST cross-region-transfer 'proposal' which lives in a press release/interview rather than a paper section (the load-bearing fact — RECAST did NOT demonstrate transfer — is robustly an absence across the paper, ADS abstract, and downstream literature). The Zhan NMRP full text was paywalled (HTTP 402); load-bearing facts came from consistent abstract extractions plus the explicit future-work section. The single most important framing guardrail, established by SafeNet (a Nature Scientific Reports paper that DID do cross-region transfer for forecasting and beat ETAS): do NOT claim 'first transfer learning for earthquake forecasting' unqualified — the defensible, evidence-backed claim is 'first neural POINT-PROCESS / point-process-LIKELIHOOD forecaster to transfer across tectonic regimes and beat region-fitted ETAS on temporal log-likelihood.' Sub-claim 5 (global-embedding memorization) is the weakest-evidenced: the research surfaced no source addressing it either way, so it cannot be affirmatively called 'first' yet. Transfer learning being well-established for phase-picking/detection/denoising/magnitude/ground-motion is real but out of scope and must be explicitly distinguished in the manuscript to preempt reviewer confusion. Venue recommendation is a judgment call, not a literature finding: the transfer/foundation-model headline + multi-regime breadth is plausibly Nature Communications / Nature Geoscience / Science Advances material, but acceptance there hinges on the spatial concession being framed as deliberate scoping and on the multi-seed significance holding up; GRL, JGR Solid Earth, and Seismica are realistic high-quality fallbacks.
openQuestions: Sub-claim 5: Is the 'global whole-catalog embedding causes memorization (train LL collapses, test LL explodes)' finding genuinely first? No source in the verified set addresses it — needs a targeted search of NPP/seismicity preprints AND the general ML literature on global/conditional embeddings causing memorization in autoregressive/generative models before it can be claimed as novel.

Does any 2026 EarthArXiv/arXiv preprint (especially from the Dascher-Cousineau/Berkeley undergraduate team noted as 'training earthquake catalogs on multiple regions') now demonstrate cross-region NPP transfer? RECAST's authors flagged this as active work; a fresh May-June 2026 sweep is needed to confirm no one has published the transfer result first.

Is the user's claimed multi-seed statistical significance of the temporal-LL win robust enough to survive review, given the benchmark already concedes NPPs are 'marginally better' in isolated cases (SCEDC higher magnitude thresholds)? The novelty leans heavily on significance + all-five-catalog consistency, which reviewers will scrutinize.

Could SafeNet-style reviewers argue the contribution is 'incremental over SafeNet' by collapsing the classifier-vs-point-process distinction? A crisp head-to-head framing (point-process likelihood vs gridded annual-max classification; per-event temporal forecasting vs annual regional max magnitude) is needed to defend the boundary.

refuted.claim: RECAST beats ETAS on temporal forecasting ONLY for large catalogs (>~10^4 events), and only slightly; for small/data-poor catalogs ETAS is better. This is the opposite of the user's data-efficiency-via-transfer claim and means RECAST does NOT beat ETAS in data-poor regions.

The neural point process does NOT broadly beat ETAS on real-catalog forecasting: at standard magnitude thresholds (e.g., above M3) the two models perform similarly, and the neural model only outperforms ETAS at a lowered threshold (M1.2) where data incompleteness penalizes ETAS.

As of Sept 2025, the EarthquakeNPP authors (Stockman, Werner) studied NPPs on a China (CENC) catalog only by re-training/adapting DeepSTPP per-catalog with seismologically-informed design choices, NOT via cross-region transfer learning or a pre-trained transferable model. No transfer-learning or foundation-model approach for forecasting is reported.

The EarthquakeNPP benchmark found that none of the five neural point process (NPP) models tested outperform ETAS on either log-likelihood or generative evaluation metrics, across the benchmark's California catalogs. This means as of this benchmark's publication, no NPP had beaten ETAS even on temporal likelihood, making the user's claim of beating ETAS temporally with multi-seed significance across all 5 California catalogs a direct, first-of-its-kind contradiction of the established benchmark baseline.
